What is the current status of: ADEME wild-dumping study, PMCB 2027 final texts, Senat PPL 24-079, AMF/CAPEB <=10m3 fund?

facts.subject: CNIL LAPI retention rules
facts.value: CNIL doctrine: LAPI data without a positive match are kept max 15 days from collection (CSI L.233-2); matched data 1 month; ACVR road-rule LAPI data are deleted once the vehicle is compliant, else max 8 working days. ALPR at decheteries must follow the same pattern.

facts.subject: CNIL badge access-log retention
facts.value: CNIL workplace-access doctrine: access-journalisation data should be deleted 3 months after recording; identification data kept while the habilitation is active, up to 5 years intermediate archive when used for time tracking.

facts.subject: Lyon Pass Decheterie quota legal framing
facts.value: Metropole de Lyon FAQ grounds its vehicle-category quotas in the dechets assimiles regime (CGCT L2224-14): PTAC<=2t vans free but 4 visits/month; PTAC>2t paid, 4 visits/month, 10 purchases/month, 50/year per usager; >3.5t banned. Quotas are justified as limiting the service to household-comparable waste financed by TEOM.

facts.subject: Rennes decheterie exploitation contract procedure
facts.value: BOAMP avis 25-65097 (11/06/2025): Rennes Metropole 'Exploitation du reseau des decheteries et plateformes de vegetaux' was published as a formal attributed contract (identifiant 2025-2520158), contradicting the SITREVA 'negotiated without publicity' concern for the current-generation contract.

facts.subject: PMCB refondation calendar
facts.value: FNTP (02/07/2026): PMCB refondation decrees/arretes in finalisation, publication expected end of August 2026, first effect 01/09/2026; new eco-org agrements 01/01/2027; matures leave free take-back 01/01/2027; FNTP CE recours claims 34 M€ undue 2024 ecocontributions; some suppliers already raising ecocontributions pre-refondation for treasury.

facts.subject: ADEME wild-dumping study status
facts.value: ADEME national wild-dumping study launched 20/05/2026 with Ecogeos + Rudologia; collectivites invited to respond (prefecture Eure 06/07/2026); results not yet published as of 31/08/2026 — the article's causal chain (access control -> wild dumping) must cite it as pending.

facts.subject: PPL fire-risk fund status
facts.value: Senat PPL (rapport l24-367) creating a compensation fund for waste-treatment fire damage from lithium battery ignition was adopted by the Senat in first reading (06/03/2026 seance); text still in parliamentary navette as of 31/08/2026, no enacted fund.

scope.lead_question: Are the three open legal frappes (RGPD badge-data retention, L2224-14 equality vs vehicle quotas, SITREVA procurement legality) valid to raise in the article, and what is the status of the four awaited publications (ADEME wild-dumping study, PMCB 2027 final texts, Senat PPL 24-079, <=10m3 fund)?

sections.ACTOR_NETWORK_MAP: CNIL (regulator, doctrine + deliberations 2024-042/043) | Ministry of Interior (STCL owner) | collectivites/EPCI (data controllers, quota setters) | access-control vendors (processors; SICTIAM = practitioner union guidance) | Metropole de Lyon (operator documenting quota rationale) | Rennes Metropole (buyer, BOAMP-published exploitation contract) | FNTP (industry litigant, CE recours 34 M€) | Senat (PPL fire fund, l24-367) | ADEME/Ecogeos/Rudologia (pending wild-dumping study) | Defenseur des droits (access-to-rights oversight).

COGNITIVE_MAP.text: Corpus: 2 CNIL official pages (family A), 1 CNIL retention guide, 1 doctrine.fr rendering of deliberation 2024-042, 1 SICTIAM practitioner guidance, 1 operator FAQ (Lyon), 1 Legifrance code article, 1 Defenseur des droits report page, 1 BOAMP notice, 1 FNTP industry position, 1 Senat report, 1 prefecture notice. Strong official core; SICTIAM is the only decheterie-specific guidance found.

CONTRADICTION_LEDGER.text: No contradictions found between sources. CNIL 2024-042 (15-day STCL retention) and the CNIL LAPI page (8 working days for ACVR road-rule systems) cover different regimes, not a conflict.

CREDO.text: If access control is now the dominant decheterie regime, its legal perimeter (data retention, equal treatment, procurement) determines whether the friction is lawful policy or unmanaged risk. The article must distinguish documented doctrine from transposition.

DIALECTICAL_MAP.text: Institutional steelman: quotas protect a TEOM-funded household service and Lyon documents the assimilated-waste reasoning. Adversarial steelman: no decheterie-specific CNIL referential exists, so retention practice varies by collectivite; equal-treatment doctrine has never been tested against quotas in court; the SITREVA concern is only partially resolved for the current contract.

EDI_REPORT.text: Corpus diversity: official regulator (CNIL), codified law (Legifrance), parliamentary (Senat), industry (FNTP), practitioner union (SICTIAM), operator (Lyon), public-records (BOAMP), independent audit (Defenseur des droits). Adequate diversity for the three legal frappes; decheterie-specific evidence remains thin (1 practitioner source).

sections.IMPACT_MAP: Article impact: (1) retention frappe — article can assert CNIL baselines with modalisation 'transposed from workplace/parking doctrine, no decheterie-specific referential'; (2) quota frappe — article can state quotas rest on the assimilated-waste legal basis and are defensible, with no litigation found (gap named); (3) procurement frappe — current-generation Rennes contract is publicly advertised, so the SITREVA concern must be scoped to the historic award only; (4) all four awaited publications confirmed still pending as of 31/08/2026, so the article cites them as pending, not as results.

MANIPULATION_REPORT.text: INPUT_KIND: TOPIC | MISSION_MODE: INVESTIGATION | SYMBOL_STAGE: CORPUS_FINAL | Official sources dominate (A-family); SICTIAM is a practitioner union (D). No marketing narratives detected in inspected sources except the Lyon FAQ, which is operator self-description and was treated as family A with its interest noted.

NEXT_QUERIES.text: Re-check after publication events: PMCB decree JORF publication, ADEME study release, PPL second reading, <=10m3 fund decision.

sections.RESOURCE_FLOW_MAP: Money/data flows touched by the three frappes: (1) passage data (badge id, plate, timestamps) flows from gate hardware to vendor platform to collectivite dashboard; retention governed by RGPD art.5(1)(e) — CNIL baselines: 3 months for access journalisation, 15 days unmatched LAPI, 1 month matched (CSI L.233-2), 8 working days ACVR. (2) TEOM funds the household service; the dechets assimiles regime (CGCT L2224-14) is the legal boundary justifying paid/quota access for utility vehicles (Lyon: free <=2t 4 visits/mo, paid >2t 4 visits/mo, banned >3.5t). (3) Public procurement value flows through advertised contracts — Rennes exploitation contract published as BOAMP 25-65097 (11/06/2025).
sections.RESPONSIBILITY_MAP: Collectivites/EPCI: responsible controllers for badge/plate data (must set + publish retention); access-control vendors: processors under contract; CNIL: doctrine + enforcement; Metropole de Lyon: documented quota rationale (model transparency); Rennes Metropole: procurement publicity compliance (BOAMP); FNTP: CE recours on PMCB ecocontribution; Senat/Assembly: PPL navette; ADEME: pending study owner.

SCOPING_REPORT.text: OBJECT_QUESTION: what does the legal/regulatory record establish about decheterie access-control data retention, quota equality, procurement legality, and the status of pending regulatory outputs as of 31/08/2026? LEAD_QUESTION: which of the three open legal frappes can the article assert, and with what strength?

VERIFICATION_REPORT.text: All 7 facts verified against inspected official or independent sources. Every fact carries >=1 FETCH-inspected source. Refutation searches found no contradicting evidence; tiers capped at ✧ where a single provenance family supports the fact.
